summary: Telegram bot client library — static patterns matched without confirmed installer harm
details: node-telegram-sockets is a Telegram Bot API client library. a static rule matched on keyword co-occurrence: the strings 'ping' appear in lib/telegram.js, src/telegram.js, and test/telegram.js (consistent with the Telegram Bot API method names such as 'getChat', 'pinChatMessage', or chat 'ping' handlers, not an OS ping invocation), and lib/telegramWebHook.js / src/telegramWebHook.js compose `require('fs')` + `require('http'/'https')` + `fs.readFileSync(...)` (the standard shape of an HTTPS webhook server that loads a TLS cert/key from disk and serves an Express-style endpoint). No lifecycle scripts (preinstall/install/postinstall) were observed; no hardcoded non-Telegram exfiltration endpoint, no credential-path read (no ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, no env-var enumeration), no obfuscation, no dropper, no install-time fetch+execute. The pattern-match signals do not, on their face, demonstrate installer harm, but contextual tracing of the flagged code paths is needed to confirm the readFileSync targets are caller-supplied cert paths and the network destinations are limited to api.telegram.org / caller-configured webhooks.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
